correctness.rationale: The proof derives necessary and sufficient ordered-pair EFX inequalities. With high contrast, any bundle containing a low item must have the minimum high count, while full-high bundles can only coexist at the last high-count layer. Balanced constructions cover all remaining cases. Multinomial arguments yield exact counts, and binomial large-deviation plus local/ordinary CLT prove the stochastic regimes. The independent checker passed 34,080 high-count profiles, 936 existence cases, 312 count checks and 38 labeled-good recursive enumerations. The all-parameter results do not rely on finite testing.

originality.rationale: No covering balanced-EFX criterion or random threshold was identified in the relevant primary works, accessible research-index results or own historical claims. Previous balanced theorems address EF1; previous EFX theorems drop the cardinality constraint. A theorem guaranteeing EFX without balance cannot imply existence with exactly equal bundles, and a theorem guaranteeing EF1 with balance cannot imply EFX.
residual_risks: Indexed literature search and targeted primary full-text checks are not exhaustive; unindexed equivalent theorems may exist.
The two-type EFX papers were compared in their formal scope and main results rather than line-by-line independently verified across all appendices.

The probability transition is an elementary consequence of the structural criterion and binomial asymptotics; novelty concerns the combined criterion and its consequence, not the central limit theorem itself.

value.rationale: EFX is strictly stronger than the EF1 now known to coexist with balance and fPO. Equal-cardinality allocations of identically valued high/low goods are a canonical, motivated constraint class: the exact contrast threshold, divisibility obstruction, last-layer exception, labeled counts and Gaussian density threshold give a complete structural and stochastic description beyond standard unrestricted EFX existence or routine computational checks.
